title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to test whether constrained prompting plus a deterministic verifier-guided generate→verify→repair loop (one allowed repair) increases deterministic-verifier semantic-correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level device configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents sampled deterministically, execution semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial sample per intent reused across conditions), model = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, guarded pipeline permitted ≤1 repair call. Results (artifact-grounded): baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.006667 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Provider accounting: completed episodes = 300; model_calls_used = 151; repair-stage invocations = 1. Interpretation: on this preregistered synthetic corpus and under shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded workflow produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline. We highlight a methodological lesson: preregistered NetOps trials require baseline-calibration pilots to avoid ceiling effects that invalidate preregistered power assumptions. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the supplied execution bundle referenced by the execution manifest.

sections.introduction: Natural-language intent interfaces aim to reduce operator burden by letting humans express desired network changes as free text that is automatically translated into executable device configurations. Prior work shows single-pass LLM outputs often contain syntactic errors, omissions, or semantic violations that can produce unsafe or unavailable states if applied without checking. A common mitigation is a generate→verify→repair architecture: the model proposes a candidate, a deterministic verifier checks intent-level invariants, and a repair stage attempts correction before execution. Building on recent verifier-integration and IaC-repair studies, we preregistered a confined confirmatory question: does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase verifier-level semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation versus an unconstrained baseline under a paired design? We executed a preregistered paired trial (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) with deterministic task generation and a strict execution contract enforcing shared_initial_candidate semantics. Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered, artifactized paired confirmatory trial with N=150 paired intents and deterministic-verifier endpoints; (2) artifact-backed numeric outcomes showing a negligible guarded benefit over an already near-ceiling baseline (baseline 149/150 → guarded 150/150; exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]); (3) an explicit methodological recommendation that preregistered NetOps trials include baseline-calibration pilots and that experimental semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent sampling) be preregistered because they materially change the estimand and interpretation.
sections.related_work: Prior literature spans intent-translation evaluations, generate→verify→repair systems, formal network verifiers, and security analyses of agentic LLM pipelines. Intent-driven translation studies report modest semantic-correctness in free-text settings and emphasize sensitivity to prompt design and verifier choice. Work that integrates deterministic verification (or verifier-guided training) has shown improved practical correctness for IaC and configuration-repair tasks, but effect sizes depend on baseline competence, verifier expressiveness, sampling semantics, and repair budgets. Mature formal-verification tools (NetKAT/KATch family and related engines) can deterministically validate reachability/isolation and policy constraints and serve as practical gating oracles, though their protocol and scale support vary. Security analyses warn that unguarded agentic pipelines can convert false textual claims into harmful actions and motivate auditable deterministic gating. Our trial situates within this literature by (a) preregistering a paired design, (b) enforcing shared_initial_candidate semantics so that the guarded–baseline contrast measures marginal repair effect on an identical sampled candidate, and (c) using a deterministic verifier as the strict binary oracle.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study was preregistered as study_cand_2026_b2_v1 with a frozen analysis plan executed before any model outputs were observed. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated with an exact two-sided McNemar test on deterministic-verifier pass/fail outcomes. Confirmatory sample: N=150 distinct synthetic intents drawn deterministically from the preregistered generator; inclusion/exclusion rules (rule-based ambiguity detector and verifier-coverage checks) were applied deterministically prior to model calls; planned episodes = 300 (150 intents × 2 conditions). The preregistration targeted detecting an absolute +15 percentage-point improvement with ≈80% power under conservative assumptions; this power target is reported and discussed below in light of observed baseline rates.

Execution semantics and the preregistration-to-execution mapping. The adapter enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent the execution adapter produced exactly one initial model generation and that identical sampled candidate was used in the paired evaluation of both baseline (A) and guarded (C) conditions. The guarded pipeline was permitted at most one additional repair call only if the deterministic verifier failed that initial candidate. The preregistration listed a conceptual three-condition design and two confirmatory hypotheses: H1 (constrained prompting vs baseline) and H2 (guarded vs constrained). Mapping from preregistration labels to the executed contrasts is explicit and concise: the archived run implements the paired contrast guarded (C) vs baseline (A) under shared_initial_candidate semantics (primary estimand). Constrained-only (B) was not executed as an independent first-pass condition in this run because the adapter reused the single initial candidate across conditions; therefore no B-vs-A or C-vs-B confirmatory contrasts based on independent first-pass samples are reported in the archived analysis. This mapping was fixed prior to execution and is reflected in the execution manifest and provider accounting.

Model, sampling, and deterministic validator. Declared model in the execution metadata: gpt-5-mini (provider record: openai_responses). The recorded execution/model_configuration.json declares declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset); because no numeric temperature or fixed random-seed was enforced, model outputs may be nondeterministic across independent API sessions. Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) applied the full_intent_constraint_validation rule and returned a boolean pass/fail verdict plus normalized final-configuration text and per-episode diagnostics; these deterministic verdicts constituted the binary endpoint for the confirmatory test.

Task corpus, prechecks, and adapter enforcement. Confirmatory tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and stratified across four intent families (reachability/isolation, ACL-like changes, VLAN/MTU sequences, uplink switchover). Topologies were limited to verifier-capable small networks (4–32 nodes). Parser and mapping unit-tests required by the preregistration passed prior to batch execution; the adapter enforced session isolation and contamination checks. The execution manifest records completed_episode_count = 300, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 150, repair: 1}, and no contamination flags.

Analysis plan and handling of incomplete pairs. Primary analysis used the exact two-sided McNemar test on the paired contingency (n_11, n_10, n_01, n_00) with a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI computed using 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Confirmatory handling of incomplete pairs followed the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule (exclude incomplete pairs from the primary test). Secondary contrasts and multiplicity corrections were preregistered but are not reported here as independent-condition comparisons because the adapter enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and constrained repair budgets at execution.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and provider audit. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150. Provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 151; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 151. Stage-level counts recorded by the adapter: shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair = 1. No contamination flags or pre-execution unit-test failures occurred; contamination_summary.csv is empty.

Primary numerical outcomes. Paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline): n_11 = 149, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). These values are reported verbatim from archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv).

Repair diagnostics and iteration counts. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150), consistent with the near-ceiling initial success rate. That single repair converted a single initially failing candidate to a verifier pass. Median revision iterations for guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Validator traces (validation_before/validation_after, normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes) are archived for each episode; representative traces for tasks 000001–000006 are included in the execution bundle.

Sensitivity and missingness. The preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats missing guarded outputs as failures was not invoked because failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0 and unscorable episodes = 0. No confirmatory exclusions occurred and the missingness_summary shows complete_pairs = 150. The paired analysis therefore used all preregistered confirmatory pairs.
sections.discussion:
Ceiling effect, power, and inferential consequence. The preregistered power calculation assumed a substantially lower baseline (target detectable effect = +15 percentage points). Observed baseline_success_rate = 0.9933 left almost no headroom for the guarded repair to show a large absolute improvement, producing a ceiling effect that invalidated the original power assumption and reduced the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit. With n_11 = 149 and only one discordant pair, the paired analysis contains very little discordant information; the exact McNemar p = 1.0 and bootstrap CI including zero reflect this paucity of discordance. This outcome underscores the preregistered methodological recommendation: include a small baseline-calibration pilot (e.g., 20–40 tasks sampled from the planned generator and prompt style) to estimate baseline competence and adjust final N or task difficulty before confirmatory sampling.

Why baseline was high and practical implications. Representative task traces show many intents contained tightly specified required sequences and constrained allowed_touched_fields; when intents are tightly specified and verifier coverage matches invariants, a single sampled candidate from a capable LLM can satisfy the verifier. In such low-ambiguity synthetic corpora a guarded repair budget of one has limited marginal opportunity to improve correctness. Practically, researchers and practitioners should align task-generator ambiguity, sampling semantics, and repair budgets with deployment expectations: if systems will act on a single first-pass candidate, shared_initial_candidate is the correct estimand; if systems will re-sample or ensemble, independent-sampling or multi-draw semantics better estimate deployed behavior.

Operational cost and diminishing returns. Provider accounting (model_calls_used = 151; repair invocations = 1) quantifies the operational cost under the one-repair policy. When baseline competence is high, the marginal cost per observed conversion is high because repairs are rarely invoked. Evaluating diminishing returns requires multi-arm experiments varying repair counts and sampling semantics; our archived artifacts include code and seeds to reproduce such arms.

Validity threats and scope. Internal validity: adapter-enforced call budgets, session isolation, and mapping unit-tests mitigate cross-condition leakage and parser-induced mis-evaluations. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier pass/fail is an operational proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; any unmodeled invariant would not be captured. External validity: experiments used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic tasks on small topologies (4–32 nodes); results do not generalize to larger heterogeneous networks or other models. Security: adversarial prompt-injection was outside this confirmatory run and remains an independent risk requiring targeted adversary-driven evaluation. Conclusion validity: the mismatch between preregistered detectable-effect assumptions and observed baseline highlights the need for pilot calibration to preserve inferential validity.

Practical prescriptions. Based on artifact-grounded outcomes we recommend: (1) a brief baseline-calibration pilot to estimate baseline_success_rate and discordant-pair proportions before final N selection; (2) preregistration and explicit reporting of generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent sampling) and repair budgets; (3) multi-arm designs that vary repair budgets and sampling semantics to estimate cost–benefit trade-offs; (4) inclusion of provider-call accounting in power and cost planning; (5) staged scaling of verifier coverage and topology size with deterministic unit-tests for mapping code. The archived execution manifest and representative tasks provide seeds and runnable code to implement these prescriptions reproducibly.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting with constrained-template prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a deterministic synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically tiny and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The principal scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials should include baseline calibration to avoid ceiling effects and preserve statistical power. Technically, our artifacts bound the marginal benefit of a one-repair guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics; evaluating independent-sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, model diversity, and production-scale topologies remains important future work.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
